claim: Crystalline Si nanoparticles have a critical diameter of about 150 nm: below it particles neither cracked nor fractured on first lithiation; above it they formed surface cracks and then fractured.
quantity_bounded: Si particle diameter (3D, single crystalline particle)
threshold_or_direction: ~150 nm; larger -> higher fracture risk (direction for us)
applies_if: Isolated crystalline Si nanoparticles, in-situ TEM, first lithiation.
cannot_cover: Batch acceptance limit; 2D section diameters of agglomerates; SiOx vs Si; cycled electrodes.
inferred: Our class-2 median equivalent diameter 8.4 px (0.21 um if 25 nm/px) and p90 41 px (~1.0 um) are above 150 nm; 150 nm = 6 px is at our segmentation floor (20 px min component ~ 5 px diameter), so L1 cannot discriminate batches here; direction only.

claim: Fracture of crystalline Si nanopillars during lithiation is anisotropic and size dependent (pillar diameter), confirming a size effect independent of Liu 2012.
threshold_or_direction: direction: larger Si features fracture more readily; exact critical diameter not found in abstract
applies_if: Crystalline Si pillars with known orientation.
cannot_cover: A numeric cutoff for our images; the exact value was not found in the accessible abstract.
observed: Anisotropic, size-dependent fracture of Si nanopillars (abstract).
inferred: Supports L1 direction only.

claim: In graphite-Si composite electrodes the gap (detachment distance) between Si particles and the carbon-black/binder domain grows with particle radius and with cycle number; detachment electrically isolates particles and drives capacity fade.
quantity_bounded: Si-matrix detachment gap and detached-particle fraction
threshold_or_direction: increases with particle radius and cycle number; no universal cutoff
applies_if: Si/graphite composite electrodes; X-ray tomographic microscopy plus BSE-SEM cross-sections; binder domain separately segmented.
cannot_cover: Our 3-class masks have no binder class; dark rims around class-2 particles may be pores, binder, or preparation artefacts.
observed: Fig. 2 (gap formation after 1, 5, 10 cycles), Fig. 3 (detachment vs radius), Results section on carbon black-binder domain detachment.
inferred: D1 candidate feature = dark rim around class-2 particle; only "investigate" after artefact review; never a verdict on its own.

claim: Müller et al. fitted an adhesion parameter kappa_0 ~ 0.02 um with upper bound < 0.05 um in their detachment model.
threshold_or_direction: model parameter only; not an image threshold
applies_if: Their five-phase segmentation and mechanical model.
cannot_cover: Direct comparison with our void-rim widths.
observed: kappa_0 ~ 0.02 um, < 0.05 um (Results after Fig. 4; Supplementary Note 11).
inferred: Not used as a bound.

claim: Chae et al. review graphite/Si co-utilisation for commercial cells; no numeric commercial Si wt% range was found in the accessible abstract.
quantity_bounded: Si mass fraction in commercial Si/graphite anodes
threshold_or_direction: not found in accessible text
applies_if: Mass-fraction data are available from the manufacturer.
cannot_cover: The draft "3-10 wt%" range: not confirmed from this source.
inferred: Draft L3 range is NOT supported by this citation; replaced by L3b/L3c direction.

claim: Battery manufacturers have introduced small amounts of Si (<6-8 wt%) into graphite anodes; SiOx blends are usually < 10 wt%.
quantity_bounded: Si (or SiOx) mass fraction in commercial anodes
threshold_or_direction: < 6-8 wt% Si; SiOx < 10 wt% (direction: low loading)
cannot_cover: Converting class-2 area fraction to wt% (needs phase identity, densities, isotropy, binder/CB accounting).
observed: "battery manufacturers have introduced small amounts of Si (<6-8 wt.%)"; "SiOx < 10 wt.%" (Introduction).
inferred: If class 2 = Si, Delesse holds, and bulk densities Si 2.33 / graphite 2.2 g cm-3 are assumed, class-2 area 0.09 of a 0.92 solid fraction gives ~10 wt% of solids: at or above this range. Every assumption is unverified, so this is a flag to confirm composition with Polaron, not a verdict.
source_locator: Introduction paragraph on Si-Gr anodes; Nat Commun 12:5459 (2021).

claim: Graphite-silicon composite negative electrodes typically contain 5-20 wt% Si (statement in the introduction of a primary paper).
threshold_or_direction: 5-20 wt% typical in research composites
cannot_cover: Commercial specification.
observed: "5-20 wt.% of silicon is added to graphitic negative electrodes" (Introduction).
inferred: Our inferred ~10 wt% (see L3b assumptions) is inside this range.

claim: A 2022 teardown of a 78 Ah automotive pouch cell found a silicon-free graphite anode.
quantity_bounded: Si mass fraction in a commercial anode
threshold_or_direction: 0 wt% Si exists in production cells
cannot_cover: A lower bound on Si content for all commercial anodes.
observed: "Silicon-free graphite was used as the anode active material" (abstract).
inferred: No universal lower bound on Si content; the draft lower limit of 3 wt% is dropped.

claim: Calendering compacts electrodes and changes density/porosity and electrochemical properties; no universal 25-40 % porosity window was found in the accessible record of Meyer et al.
threshold_or_direction: direction: calendering lowers porosity; numeric window not found
applies_if: Electrodes processed as in the paper.
cannot_cover: The draft 25-40 % window as a literature bound.
inferred: Draft L4 becomes direction-only; see L4b-L4d for the only numbers found.

claim: For graphite electrodes (8 wt% binder, 4 wt% conductive additive) a compression rate of 10 % was beneficial for long-term cycling; stronger compaction deforms active material and changes specific pore-size ranges.
threshold_or_direction: moderate compaction (10 % compression) beneficial; over-compaction harmful
cannot_cover: A porosity number for our electrode.
observed: Compression rate of 10 % identified as beneficial (abstract).
inferred: Direction only.

claim: Direct 3D X-ray tomography of a graphite electrode gave pore volume fraction 0.484; slice-wise 2D area fractions ranged 0.443-0.531 (max under/over-estimation 8.6 % / 9.8 %).
quantity_bounded: graphite electrode pore fraction and its 2D sampling scatter
threshold_or_direction: reference value 0.484 (one electrode); 2D single-slice error up to ~10 % relative
applies_if: Uncalendered research graphite electrode imaged by synchrotron X-ray tomography at micrometre resolution.
cannot_cover: Our class 0 (0.10) is a BSE grey-level class at 25 nm/px that lumps pores, binder/CB and sub-resolution material; not the same quantity.
observed: Table 3: Graphite 3D 0.484; x/y/z 2D means 0.484, SD 0.005-0.013, min 0.443, max 0.531.
inferred: Our class-0 area 0.10 is far below this and below the draft 25-40 %; the difference is more plausibly segmentation/phase-lumping or resin-filled pores than a material fact -> investigate reason, not a verdict.

claim: FIB-SEM of porous materials exposes sub-surface pore walls whose grey levels overlap with the solid, complicating pore segmentation.
threshold_or_direction: direction: FIB-SEM pore fractions from grey-level thresholds are biased
applies_if: Porous, poorly conducting samples imaged by FIB-SEM.
cannot_cover: A correction factor for our class-0 fraction.
observed: Overlap of grey levels between solid and pore areas (abstract).
inferred: Explains why class-0 fraction cannot be read as porosity without validation.

claim: Inhomogeneities from nanoscale to mesoscale (composition, porosity, particle size, contact) can reduce Li-ion battery durability.
threshold_or_direction: direction: more harmful heterogeneity -> worse durability; no numeric cutoff
applies_if: Heterogeneity KPI defined on an image and compared within one electrode design.
cannot_cover: Numeric threshold or causal proof from our images.
inferred: Report tile-to-tile dispersion (SD/IQR of fractions) per image as a KPI; direction only.

claim: Simulated electrodes with microstructural heterogeneity (porosity/thickness variation) show degraded performance relative to homogeneous ones.
threshold_or_direction: direction only
cannot_cover: Threshold for our images.
inferred: Direction only.

claim: Particle shape and fabrication-induced alignment produce tortuosity anisotropy in Li-ion electrodes.
threshold_or_direction: direction: alignment changes through-plane vs in-plane transport
applies_if: Through-plane direction known in the image.
cannot_cover: Our image axes are not confirmed relative to the current-collector normal; 2D chord anisotropy is not tortuosity.
inferred: Report a 2D orientation/anisotropy KPI only as a within-dataset comparison.

claim: Magnetically aligning graphite flakes in model anodes increased lithium storage capacity at practical charging rates by a factor 1.6-3 relative to a conventional reference.
threshold_or_direction: direction: alignment matters; 1.6-3x at high rate in model anodes
cannot_cover: Translating a 2D orientation index into a pass/fail bound.
observed: Factor 1.6-3 (corrigendum text, Nature Energy 2:17061 (2017), which updates the last sentence of the article).
inferred: Direction only.

claim: Electrode/separator tortuosity can be measured by impedance spectroscopy and compared with microstructural estimates.
threshold_or_direction: method/reference only
cannot_cover: Any value from our images.
inferred: Not applicable to image-only QC.

claim: Si/graphite electrodes show distinct degradation phenomena (Si vs graphite) that change with cycling; Si nanoparticle morphology changes depend on cut-off potential.
threshold_or_direction: direction: cycled Si particles change size/morphology; pristine distribution should be documented
cannot_cover: A pristine particle-size bound.
inferred: Our images are presumably pristine; size distribution is a documented baseline, not a bound.

claim: Si content in Si/graphite composites affects specific capacity, cycling and ageing (systematic variation study).
threshold_or_direction: direction: more Si -> more capacity, faster fade; numbers not found in abstract
cannot_cover: A threshold for us.
inferred: Direction only.

claim: 4D operando nano-holotomography of Si-graphite electrodes resolves multiscale chemo-mechanics (preprint).
threshold_or_direction: direction only
cannot_cover: Any threshold.
inferred: Background only.

claim: Nearest-neighbour distance statistics (Clark-Evans) quantify clustering vs random dispersion of point patterns.
threshold_or_direction: method: R < 1 clustered, R = 1 random, R > 1 regular
applies_if: Particle centroids treated as a 2D point pattern within the field of view; edge effects handled.
cannot_cover: A battery-specific clustering bound (none found).
inferred: Report R per image as a KPI; compare batches only.

claim: Local thickness (largest inscribed sphere) gives a model-independent pore/strut size distribution from binary images.
threshold_or_direction: method only
applies_if: Binary pore mask; 2D version is a planar approximation.
cannot_cover: A pore-size bound for anodes (none found).
inferred: Use for class-0 and class-1 size KPIs in px; px->nm only if pixel size confirmed.

claim: Cracks, particle detachment and electrical isolation are visible in cross-sectional SEM/X-ray imaging of Si/graphite electrodes and are mechanistic degradation features.
threshold_or_direction: presence -> investigate, only after artefact review
applies_if: Feature is exposed by the cross-section and survives artefact review (curtaining, redeposition, pull-out).
cannot_cover: A verdict from a single dark cavity or line.
observed: Figs 2-3 detachment gaps; electrical isolation modelled.
inferred: Feature-1 candidate definitions; no inter-annotator agreement figure found for battery cross-sections.

claim: Microstructural cracking in Ni-rich NMC811 cathodes was identified and its origins analysed with cross-sectional imaging.
threshold_or_direction: direction: crack = intra/inter-particle discontinuity; chemistry differs from ours
cannot_cover: Anode Si/graphite crack criteria.
inferred: Vocabulary only.

claim: Foundation-model transfer enables data-efficient crack quantification in Li-ion cathode micrographs (preprint).
threshold_or_direction: method only
cannot_cover: Anode applicability; preprint requires check.
inferred: Possible Feature-1 method; not evidence.

claim: Delamination from the current collector cannot be assessed unless the collector/coating interface is in the field of view.
threshold_or_direction: not measurable in current images
cannot_cover: Any D2 verdict from the present 31 fields of view.
observed: Interface imaging in Müller et al.
inferred: D2 stays unmeasured; recorded as not_applicable in the ledger.

claim: FIB milling produces curtaining (vertical, thin, uneven bands caused by milling through phases of different density) and charging halos; both are imaging artefacts, not structure.
threshold_or_direction: artefact present -> treat as covariate, not defect
cannot_cover: Proof that a given dark line is artefactual.
observed: Section 1-2: curtaining "appear as vertical, thin, uneven bands"; charging from insulating samples.
inferred: Vertical line features aligned with the milling direction are excluded from crack candidates unless they cross phase boundaries irregularly.

claim: FIB milling causes redeposition, implantation and amorphisation; preparation can alter soft materials chemically and mechanically.
threshold_or_direction: direction: artefact classes to exclude from defect calls

source_locator: Abstract; Micron 30:197-204 (1999); see also Bassim 2011 J. Microsc. 245:288-301.

claim: Inter-observer variability of manual delineation is substantial even for experts (medical CT study).
threshold_or_direction: direction: expect disagreement; measure it (Cohen kappa or Dice) before using defect labels
cannot_cover: Battery-specific agreement figures (none found).

claim: Hotelling T2 charts for individual observations need an exact (beta-based) start-up limit; approximate F/chi-square limits are conservative in Phase I.
threshold_or_direction: joint deviation beyond a pre-registered reference envelope
applies_if: Image-level feature vectors; reference set defined before evaluation.
cannot_cover: Normal-theory limits at n = 17 with p close to n; use permutation / LOO.
observed: Exact beta-distribution limits for Phase I individuals charts (abstract).
inferred: Report T2 with image-level permutation null band.

claim: When parameters are estimated from a small reference sample, T2 chart performance degrades; corrected limits and sample-size recommendations exist.
threshold_or_direction: direction: n = 17 reference images is far below recommended sizes
cannot_cover: Our non-normal, small-n setting; treat limits as heuristics.
observed: Corrected limits for small reference samples (abstract).
inferred: Any T2 limit is a screening heuristic; final calibration must be image-level permutation.

claim: Robust estimators (e.g. MCD) of location and scatter reduce masking of outliers in Phase I multivariate charts.
threshold_or_direction: use robust reference + LOO screening
applies_if: Contamination of the reference batch possible (Batch_3 not guaranteed clean).
cannot_cover: Proof that the reference is clean.
observed: Robust T2 for individuals (abstract); FAST-MCD algorithm: Rousseeuw & Van Driessen 1999.
inferred: Compute both classical and MCD-based distances; disagreement -> investigate.

claim: Hierarchical/multi-level data must be resampled at the cluster level; treating nested observations as independent inflates false positives (>45 % in their simulations).
threshold_or_direction: resample images, never tiles
applies_if: Images are clusters; tiles are nested.
cannot_cover: Battery-specific thresholds; preprint status.
inferred: Bootstrap over images (n = 7/7/17); tile-level statistics are descriptive only.

claim: Energy distance and MMD are equivalent families of distance-based two-sample statistics.
threshold_or_direction: larger -> more different; calibrate by permutation
applies_if: Fixed feature representation; permutation over images.
cannot_cover: Power guarantees at n = 7.
inferred: Report statistic + permutation p + null band at image level.
source_locator: Abstract; Ann. Statist. 41(5) (2013); energy statistics: Szekely & Rizzo 2013; MMD: Gretton 2007.

claim: Permutation tests give exact finite-sample inference under exchangeability; p-values should never be reported as zero.
threshold_or_direction: exact permutation p with (b+1)/(m+1) correction
cannot_cover: Non-exchangeable acquisition groups (stratify permutations by acquisition group).
inferred: With 7 vs 17 images the minimum two-sided p is limited; report it explicitly.
source_locator: Stat. Appl. Genet. Mol. Biol. 9(1):39 (2010); Ernst 2004 Stat. Sci.

claim: Aggregated MMD tests with permutation / wild-bootstrap calibration are non-asymptotically valid (preprint).
threshold_or_direction: direction only
cannot_cover: Robustness to reference contamination.
inferred: Optional; not required for v1.

claim: One-class methods (one-class SVM, Isolation Forest) model the support of a reference distribution without anomalies in training.
threshold_or_direction: score beyond reference support -> investigate
cannot_cover: Calibration with 17 reference images (very unstable).
observed: One-class SVM definition (abstract); Isolation Forest: Liu 2008.
inferred: Use only with image-level LOO calibration.

claim: PatchCore uses a memory bank of nominal patch features for anomaly localisation (MVTec AD benchmark).
threshold_or_direction: visual localisation only; not a batch verdict
applies_if: Nominal reference tiles representative; acquisition covariates monitored.
cannot_cover: Defect truth; tile pseudoreplication; texture-induced false positives.
inferred: Patch scores aggregated per image; shown as heat maps for review only.
source_locator: CVPR 2022 pp. 14298-14308; dataset: Bergmann 2019; library: Akcay 2022.

claim: LIBAD (Li-ion electrode manufacturing anomaly benchmark) reports homogeneous electrode appearance, cross-modal inconsistency and limited transfer of anomaly detectors (preprint).
quantity_bounded: false-positive / transfer risk of anomaly maps
threshold_or_direction: direction: weak evidence only
cannot_cover: FIB-SEM specifics; any defect in our set.
inferred: Anomaly maps never upgrade a verdict alone.

claim: Conformal prediction gives distribution-free finite-sample coverage; conformal p-values enable outlier testing with FDR control.
threshold_or_direction: image outside the (1-alpha) conformal envelope of the reference -> investigate
applies_if: Exchangeable reference images; calibration set disjoint from training.
cannot_cover: With 17 reference images the finest achievable alpha is 1/18.
observed: Conformal p-values for outliers (abstract); regression version: Lei 2018; tutorial: Angelopoulos & Bates 2023.

claim: Batch effects in high-throughput data are pervasive and can be confounded with the biological/material signal of interest.
threshold_or_direction: direction: model acquisition group explicitly
applies_if: Known acquisition grouping (13 height/XResolution groups span batches).
cannot_cover: Separation of acquisition and material effects without a design.

claim: Image-based profiling pipelines aggregate per-cell features to the well/sample level and correct for plate/batch effects before comparison.
threshold_or_direction: aggregate tiles -> image before statistics
cannot_cover: Battery-specific thresholds.

claim: Unsupervised anomaly detection on in-situ layer images in laser powder-bed additive manufacturing is a published materials QC application.
threshold_or_direction: application precedent only

inferred: Precedent only.

claim: Multivariate SPC foundations (Hotelling T2, Phase I/II, interpretation of signals) are standard textbook material.

cannot_cover: Validity at n = 17 without resampling.

claim: Preregistration separates prediction from postdiction and limits analytic flexibility; undisclosed flexibility inflates false positives.
threshold_or_direction: freeze features, aggregation, thresholds before held-out images
applies_if: Plan written and hashed before opening held-out data.

claim: Benjamini-Hochberg controls the false discovery rate across multiple tests.
threshold_or_direction: report BH-adjusted and raw p-values
cannot_cover: Dependence structure between KPIs (use BY or permutation max-T if strong).

claim: Traceability is "the ability to access any or all information relating to that which is under consideration, throughout its entire life cycle, by means of recorded identifications".

claim: No-reference FIB-SEM quality indices for noise, contrast, blur, curtaining and charging; values near 0 indicate serious quality problems; curtaining index works only at higher dwell time (hidden by noise otherwise); charging index is fooled by overexposed halos.
threshold_or_direction: measure as covariates; compare within similar structures only

claim: Curtaining appears as frequency components along the horizontal frequency axis of the FFT of the x-gradient image; stripe removal literature (Münch et al.) is the basis of the curtaining index.
threshold_or_direction: FFT energy concentration near k_y = 0
cannot_cover: Stripes at other angles.

claim: Combined wavelet-Fourier filtering removes stripe/ring artefacts; the energy removed quantifies the correction.

applies_if: Stripe geometry compatible; filter parameters frozen.

claim: Charging in SEM of insulators depends on beam energy relative to the critical energy E2 and on irradiation history; it produces contrast and brightness artefacts.
threshold_or_direction: report edge_charging covariate per image
cannot_cover: A material interpretation of bright rims.

claim: Real-world SEM micrograph quality variation degrades ML robustness; quality can correlate with microscope conditions rather than material.

claim: In FIB-SEM of highly porous media, sub-surface structure shines through pores (shine-through), preventing naive grey-level segmentation; simulation and morphological methods were developed to handle it.

claim: ASTM E1245 standardises automatic image analysis of inclusion/second-phase content (area fraction, count, size) with stereological reporting.

claim: ASTM E562 estimates volume fraction by systematic manual point count on 2D sections (Delesse principle: V_V = A_A = P_P).
threshold_or_direction: only under random/isotropic sectioning assumptions
applies_if: Random or systematic sections; valid constituent classification.

claim: Stereological predictions of battery-electrode pore fraction from 2D slices matched 3D within ~10 % for graphite, but specific surface area was under-estimated by up to 52 % and varied with slicing direction.

claim: Saltykov-type unfolding converts 2D section-size distributions to 3D but assumes particle shape and sampling conditions.

claim: ImageRep predicts phase-fraction representativity (confidence interval) from a single image via the two-point correlation function; assumes macro-homogeneity (decaying correlations) and finite feature sizes; validated on battery separators among others.

claim: Tortuosity factors from tomographic data are computed with open tools (TauFactor) on 3D volumes.
threshold_or_direction: 3D only
